subject: Order Form + MSA: DPA sequencing, SCCs mapping and approval runbook
messages:
From: Ekaterina Sokolova <ekaterina@novaprod.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@novaprod.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the MSA+Order Form package and returned a focused set of redlines on the DPA and SCCs mapping. Their priority is: (1) clear assignment of controller/processor roles in the Order Form exhibit, (2) SCCs selector table so they can confirm transfer paths for EU data, and (3) a sequencing / approval runbook so procurement can close on our PO without legal having to chase multiple teams.

I attached their redline (Novaprod_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) and an SCC mapping spreadsheet. Can you confirm the cadence for internal sign-offs and whether Redwood will accept the minimal change to the MSA liability paragraph they flagged? Procurement wants to know if a 2-business-day legal review window is realistic.

Best,
Ekaterina
Legal — Novaprod Health
attachments: Novaprod_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx, 132KB), SCCs_Clause_Map.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ekaterina Sokolova <ekaterina@novaprod.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

Ekaterina, thanks for the redlines and the SCC mapping. Quick read-through attached; high-level response below. We'll aim to provide a clean DPA + SCCs table back to you with a proposed sequencing runbook for procurement.

Summary of internal owners (for clarity):
- Legal (Laura) will lead DPA redline negotiation and final signoff.
- Sales (Ben) will manage procurement expectations and commercial tradeoffs (credits/SLAs).
- Privacy & Evidence (Neha) will validate SCCs mapping and provide any required technical evidence for transfer paths / subprocessor roster.

Immediate asks for us:
1) Can Novaprod confirm which EU processing locations are in scope (AT/FR/DE)? We need that to finalize the SCCs selector.
2) Is Novaprod able to accept our existing MSA liability cap with the specific carveout for breach-related regulatory fines? That was the one commercial ask called out.

I propose a 3-step runbook we can return to procurement:
A) Laura reviews and issues comment bundle (2 business days)
B) Joint legal call to resolve 3rd-party clauses (1 hour)
C) Final countersign with Order Form executed by procurement (1 business day after final doc exchange)

If that timeline works we will aim to get a draft runbook + updated DPA back by EOD Wed (2026-11-04).

Thanks — Grace
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_DPA_Response_outline.pdf (pdf, 24KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

+1 on Grace's plan. I reviewed Novaprod_DPA_Redline_v3 and added legal comments; two things for internal alignment before we send anything back:

1) SCCs mapping: the external spreadsheet uses an untested mapping for our private deployment option. Neha — can your team confirm whether any EU routing or KMS boundaries will block Novaprod's preferred SCCs path? If so we need to call that out explicitly.

2) Liability language: Novaprod asked to narrow the liability cap carveout. There is a commercial ask here — Ben, if they push on reducing the carveout we should trade for a 12-month committed minimum on Dedicated (we may not want to do that but have it as a lever).

I'll prepare a redline that keeps our standard MSA positions but accepts two limited clarifications to the DPA: (a) an explicit list of processing locations tied to SCC selection, and (b) a short acknowledgement that Novaprod may provide additional lawful basis evidence on request.

I'll target to send the legal comment bundle by COB Tue (2026-11-03).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

Laura / Grace — quick ops check on SCCs and evidence:

- Confirmed hosting footprint: EU tenants are hosted in Frankfurt (DE) and Amsterdam (NL); we do not route EU production to AT/FR unless customer elects a region-specific hosting addendum.
- KMS/EKM boundaries: EU keys reside in our EU KMS region and are accessible per customer key policies; we can provide an encryption-at-rest statement and KMS architecture diagram for evidence.
- Subprocessor roster: current roster includes two EU subprocessors (storage provider & monitoring). I'll export a stamped roster and timeline.

Implication: Novaprod's SCC selection should target the EU-to-EU transfer path (Frankfurt/Amsterdam) — we can map that cleanly. If they insist on a different hosting territory we need their explicit region election before signoff.

Deliverables I'll attach to the comment bundle:
- SCCs_Clause_Map_filled.xlsx (with hosting columns)
- KMS_Export_Statement.pdf
- Subprocessor_Roster_20261104.csv

Neha
Staff Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: SCCs_Clause_Map_filled.xlsx (xlsx, 52KB), KMS_Export_Statement.pdf (pdf, 78KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ekaterina Sokolova <ekaterina@novaprod.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procure@novaprod.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

Ekaterina — appreciate the clear asks. Quick commercial response: we will not move the general liability cap materially, but we can be flexible on a limited carveout wording tied to regulatory fines caused by Redwood negligence. If Novaprod needs a further concession, we can discuss a modest committed capacity (6-month pilot minimum) as trade.

Operationally — Grace / Laura / Neha will share the legal bundle plus evidence items by EOD Fri (2026-11-06). Can Novaprod confirm a 48-hour review expectation once we return the cleaned DPA? Procurement indicated they can turn quickly if the SCCs table and role exhibit are final.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ekaterina Sokolova <ekaterina@novaprod.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procure@novaprod.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novaprod order form & DPA — redlines and next steps

Thanks everyone — helpful. Novaprod confirms:
- Scope: EU processing in DE/NL only.
- Procurement will accept a 48-hour legal review on the final DPA + SCCs table.
- On liability: they are prepared to accept Redwood's existing cap if we add the limited carveout language Laura suggested.

Next steps per our side: Novaprod will join a 30-minute legal call Wed 11/10 at 09:00 CET to walk the SCCs table. Can Redwood share the final redline + evidence bundle before EOD Tue (11/9)? We'll add any minor comments on a 48-hour turnaround.

Ekaterina
Novaprod Health — Legal
